candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy findings (nodular lymphocyte infiltrate, germinal centers, CD20+, BCL-2−) are consistent with cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia of B-cell type, which is the known histological correlate of actinic prurigo. However, the candidate label names only the histopathological pattern and omits the photodermatosis etiology (confirmed by delayed UV-A erythema on phototest), the clinical diagnosis of actinic prurigo, and the associated cheilitis. It is therefore a component/partial parent rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia (B-cell) describes the histopathological finding (nodular B-cell lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers, CD20+, BCL-2−) seen in this case, but does not capture the full diagnostic object: actinic prurigo with associated cheilitis. The reference diagnosis requires recognition of the photodermatosis etiology (delayed UV-A reaction on phototest), the clinical syndrome of actinic prurigo, and the characteristic cheilitis component. CLH is the reactive histological pattern underlying actinic prurigo but is not the final clinicopathological diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Actinic prurigo is a photodermatosis classically associated with HLA-DR4 (DRB1*0407) in Latin American populations; this case involves a white woman, which is less typical but not exclusionary.
Cheilitis is a hallmark feature of actinic prurigo and is explicitly present in the clinical record, reinforcing the reference diagnosis.
CLH B-cell pattern on biopsy is the known histological substrate of actinic prurigo, making C001 a component finding rather than the final diagnosis.
